name: The Vedic course of dharma (Mīmāṃsā account)

stages.name: vedādhyayana
stages.gloss: study of one's Vedic recension from a teacher
stages.description: The student learns the Veda by the injunction of study.

stages.name: dharma-jijñāsā
stages.description: Before returning home the student inquires into the meaning of the Vedic sentences.

stages.name: agnyādhāna
stages.description: Becoming eligible (with one's wife) for the śrauta rites.

stages.name: nitya-naimittika karma
stages.description: Rites such as the Agnihotra and the new- and full-moon offerings, performed for life.

stages.name: kāmya karma
stages.description: Rites such as the Jyotiṣṭoma for one desiring heaven; their fruit comes through the apūrva.

stages.name: svarga
stages.description: The fruit of the rites, understood as happiness; the self, not the burnt body, attains it.

notes: A reconstruction of the sequence implied by the texts, not a map the tradition itself numbers. Heaven receives no band because it is not liberation; the bands are interpretive (interpretation layer).

name: Kumārila's way to release (Bhāṭṭa)

stages.name: kāmya-niṣiddha-varjana
stages.gloss: abstaining from desire-prompted and prohibited acts
stages.description: No new fruits requiring bodies are produced.

stages.name: nitya-naimittika-anuṣṭhāna
stages.description: To avoid the demerit of omission; Tantravārttika: also to destroy past sin.

stages.name: ātmajñāna
stages.description: Knowing the self (made firm by Vedānta); the self-knower no longer desires the fruits, so they do not accrue.

stages.name: bhoga (pūrvakriyākṣaya)
stages.description: Past karma is used up by experiencing its fruits.

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: With no accumulation left no body arises; for Pārthasārathi, the absolute dissolution of the threefold bond, without bliss.

notes: The order is logical rather than strictly temporal (stages 1-4 run concurrently). Band B5 for self-knowledge is at most 'analogous': Kumārila does not treat it as a liberating insight.

name: The Prābhākara way to release (Śālikanātha)

stages.name: saṃsāra-udvega
stages.gloss: aversion to the sorrows of saṃsāra
stages.description: Troubled by worldly sorrows and indifferent even to the pleasures mixed with them, one rises for release.

stages.name: niṣiddha-kāmya-nivṛtti
stages.gloss: turning from prohibited and desire-prompted acts
stages.description: Abstaining from the causes of bondage and from means to prosperity.

stages.name: bhoga
stages.description: Dharma and adharma already produced are exhausted by being experienced.

stages.name: ātmajñāna with śama, dama, brahmacarya
stages.gloss: self-knowledge supported by calm, restraint, celibacy
stages.description: Enjoined for non-return, it destroys the remaining store of karma.

stages.name: dehoccheda
stages.description: The self remains in mere being, all-pervading, without cognition or bliss.

notes: Sequence as stated in one passage; bands are interpretive.
